finding.text: The `TestRunner --near <file>` command-line mode (ask 1) is not wired up. `public/framework/core/Test/TestRunner.mjs:145` sets `n = args.indexOf("--near")` but never uses it, so `--near a.mjs` falls through to `find()` and runs `a.mjs` itself as if it were a test. Checked on the branch: `node TestRunner.mjs --near a.mjs` printed `PASS …/a.mjs`. The `near()` method is correct; it needs a branch like the `--covers` one that prints or runs `r.near(norm(args[n + 1]))`.

On a worktree's first run of a test, a failure with no earlier result is reported as a message ("fails") even though nothing changed from pass to fail (`Servex/WorktreeWatch.js:201`, `was !== false`). This only stays quiet for the ~15 tests already failing on michael/dev if results.jsonl already holds a failing line for each of them. Consider staying quiet when `was === undefined`, or seed the state from a first run.

Save runs use Servex's own TestRunner (`runner_url`), so every `trigger:"save"` line from every worktree is appended to the main tree's `core/Test/results.jsonl`. That matches "every run still appends", but it keeps a tracked main-tree file dirty and mixes worktree results with dev's. `prior()` then reads dev's latest line as the worktree's starting point.

`MergeTests.gate` runs inside the merge lock (`Server/merge.mjs:493`), so a diff covered by many tests, or one that times out at 60 s, holds up every other merge for that long. This is acceptable for now; it is worth one line in the merge doc.

The base run happens only for tests that fail on the branch (`Server/MergeTests.mjs:37`), not for every covering test as the brief says. It gives the same verdict for less work. This is the simpler way, and the reason is stated in the file header.
